record.paper_title: The Higgs program and open questions in particle physics and cosmology
record.original_question: Did CP-violating interactions of the Higgs boson h generate the baryon asymmetry of the Universe through electroweak baryogenesis? In particular, can complex Higgs Yukawa couplings, such as CP-violating hττ or htt interactions, provide the needed CP violation, and can measurements of CP-violating Higgs-coupling parameters test this possibility?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Standard Model of particle physics extended only by allowing the Yukawa couplings of the observed Higgs boson $h$ (with mass $\approx 125\,\mathrm{GeV}$) to fermions $f$ to be complex, so that the effective Lagrangian for a fermion $f$ takes the form
$$\mathcal{L}_{hff} = -g_{hff}\,h\,\bigl[\cos(\phi_f)\,\bar f f + \sin(\phi_f)\,\bar f\, i\gamma_5 f\bigr],$$
where $g_{hff}>0$ is the magnitude of the coupling and $\phi_f\in(-\pi,\pi]$ is a CP-violating mixing angle ($\phi_f=0$ corresponds to a pure CP-even, Standard-Model-like coupling, $\phi_f=\pm\pi/2$ to a pure CP-odd coupling).

Within the framework of electroweak baryogenesis (in which the observed cosmological baryon-to-photon ratio $\eta_B \simeq 6\times 10^{-10}$ is generated at a first-order electroweak phase transition through CP-violating interactions at the bubble walls), determine the following:

(a) Can a nonzero CP-violating phase $\phi_f$ in the Higgs Yukawa couplings — in particular in the $h\tau\bar\tau$ coupling ($f=\tau$) and/or the $ht\bar t$ coupling ($f=t$) — supply a CP-violating source sufficient to generate the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe, consistently with all current experimental constraints (including bounds from the electron electric dipole moment and from LHC measurements of Higgs production and decay)?

(b) Identify experimental observables involving the CP-violating mixing angles $\phi_\tau$ and $\phi_t$ whose precision measurement at present or near-future colliders would conclusively confirm or rule out this mechanism.
artifact.category_tag: Electroweak baryogenesis and Higgs CP violation
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains open. Recent analyses show that CP violation in quark Yukawa couplings is severely constrained by electron EDM bounds, but a complex τ Yukawa coupling can still by itself account for the observed baryon asymmetry within current LHC and EDM limits, while complex t or b couplings can contribute only a few percent. No experiment has yet measured a nonzero CP phase φ_τ or φ_t, and ATLAS/CMS measurements so far are consistent with φ_τ=0 with sizeable uncertainty, leaving the mechanism neither confirmed nor excluded.

status_evidence.title: A new bound on CP violation in the τ lepton Yukawa coupling and electroweak baryogenesis
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on CP violation in quark Yukawa couplings exclude their significant role in electroweak baryogenesis, but it can still be played by the τ lepton Yukawa coupling.
status_evidence.claim: Tau Yukawa CP phase can still drive EWBG; quark Yukawa CP phases largely cannot.

status_evidence.title: CP violation from τ, t and b dimension-6 Yukawa couplings — interplay of baryogenesis, EDM and Higgs physics
status_evidence.snippet: Complex τ Yukawa coupling can account for the observed baryon asymmetry within current LHC and EDM bounds; complex b (t) Yukawa coupling can account for 4% (2%).
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative viable parameter space exists for τ Yukawa-driven EWBG.

status_evidence.title: Testing aligned CP-violating Higgs sector at future lepton colliders
status_evidence.snippet: Future lepton colliders can probe CP-violating Higgs Yukawa couplings beyond current LHC sensitivity.
status_evidence.claim: Decisive tests of the mechanism require future precision Higgs CP measurements.
